findings.reason: The original standalone tiles contain the complete example and verification but no geometric illustration. A single coordinate line makes the strict inclusion of the nonnegative score ray in its real linear span immediately visible, especially the excluded vector -X; this is warranted explanatory content under the expanded diagram scope.
findings.action: Added a final Remarks section defining X(x)=x and a fenced TikZ coordinate-line picture, highlighting the nonnegative score ray and marking -X, 0 and X.

correction: Appended explanatory Remarks and a score-cone versus full-tangent-line illustration; all original source bytes are retained as the unchanged prefix.

diagram_math_checks.objects: The ambient real mean-zero space on the equiprobable two-point law is L^2_0(P_0)={bX:b in R}, with X(x)=x.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Example and verification step 4.1; def-mean-zero-square-integrable-space defines the mean-zero quotient space. Because both atoms have positive mass, bX is identified uniquely by b.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The full bidirectional line represents all real b, while the highlighted ray begins at 0 and extends only to positive b, including its origin.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 2.2 realizes each a>=0 as a path score; step 3.1 forces every score to have that form. Thus the ray is exactly the score set, rather than an arbitrary subset.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The marked points -X, 0 and X are equally spaced with coordinates -1, 0 and 1. Only 0 and X are on the highlighted ray; -X is on the ambient line.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The coordinate is b in bX, and step 4.1 explicitly establishes X is a score and -X is not.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The full ambient line is also the closed linear tangent space, not merely its unclosed span.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 4.1 uses F8 to establish closedness and F3/def-tangent-space to identify the closure of the real span. Arrowheads indicate unbounded coordinate directions, not morphisms or statistical transitions.

diagram_math_checks.proof_independence: The original five verification steps are unchanged; the diagram follows them in Remarks and provides no premise used in their rigorous argument.
